title: Taxonomy placement verdict (one record per probe run or human tap)
description: Plan section 5.2. The probe returns only path, verdict, reason, target, runner_up and note; the harness adds qid, run_id, probe_version, taxonomy_version, found and hops. A probe output that carries found or hops is an instrument defect. Cross-field rules are enforced by verdicts.py and listed under x-cross-field-rules; a record that fails either is discarded and counted as an instrument defect, never repaired.

path.description: Topics opened, in order, each `topic` or `topic/subclass`. The first segment must be a topic or view id from topics.json; the last topic is where the verdict was given.

hops.description: Harness-computed: the number of entries in path.

found.description: Harness-computed: the topic where the verdict was given equals the question's expected_topic. Never reported by the probe.

target.description: A topic id (belongs_in) or an element id from elements.json (duplicate_of, cannot_tell_apart_from).

runner_up.description: A topic or view id: the second-best home. Required unless the verdict is right_here.

note.description: One line. Required for cannot_tell: what was missing.

x-cross-field-rules: right_here: reason, target and runner_up may be null; reason must be null.
wrong_here requires a reason of missing_or_broken_here, belongs_in, duplicate_of or cannot_tell_apart_from.
belongs_in requires a target that is a topic or view id other than the topic where the verdict was given.
duplicate_of and cannot_tell_apart_from require a target that is an element id from elements.json.
cannot_tell requires a reason of missing_information, missing_context or invalid_flow, and a note.
runner_up is required, and must be a topic or view id, whenever the verdict is not right_here.
path entries start with a known topic or view id; hops equals len(path).
found is true exactly when the topic where the verdict was given equals the question's expected_topic.
